levels.title: Level 0 · Reading YAML
levels.summary: Every Kubernetes file is written in YAML. Start here if YAML is new to you.

lessons.title: Read a YAML file
lessons.summary: Learn the three rules of YAML and spot the most common indentation mistake.

lessons.title: Parts of every manifest
lessons.summary: Learn the four parts every Kubernetes file shares, and how kubectl explain describes any field.

levels.title: Level 1 · Run an app
levels.summary: Build each file one block at a time. Practise Anywhere lessons free on your laptop.

lessons.title: Run one container
lessons.summary: A Pod runs one or more containers together. It is the smallest thing Kubernetes runs.

lessons.title: Keep copies running
lessons.summary: A ReplicaSet keeps copies of a Pod running. Deployments create one for you.

lessons.title: Keep your app running
lessons.summary: A Deployment keeps the number of Pods you ask for running and replaces any that fail.

lessons.title: CPU and memory
lessons.summary: Tell Kubernetes how much CPU and memory each container needs and may use.

lessons.title: Group your work
lessons.summary: A Namespace keeps related objects together and apart from everything else in the cluster.

lessons.title: Settings outside the image
lessons.summary: A ConfigMap holds settings, so you can change them without rebuilding the container image.

lessons.title: Passwords and keys
lessons.summary: A Secret holds passwords and keys apart from normal settings, so you can limit who reads them.

lessons.title: Run a task to the end
lessons.summary: A Job runs a task until it finishes. A CronJob runs a Job on a schedule.

levels.title: Level 2 · Connect apps
levels.summary: Give your Pods stable addresses inside the cluster and open them to the internet.

lessons.title: Give your app an address
lessons.summary: A Service gives a group of Pods one stable name and address inside the cluster.

lessons.title: Find a Service by name
lessons.summary: Every Service gets a DNS name, so apps can reach each other by name.

lessons.title: A port on every node
lessons.summary: A NodePort Service opens the same port on every node in the cluster.

lessons.title: Point to an outside name
lessons.summary: An ExternalName Service gives an outside address a name inside the cluster.

lessons.title: Open your app to the internet
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an AWS Network Load Balancer in front of your Pods.

lessons.title: Route web traffic
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an AWS Application Load Balancer that routes web requests to your app.

levels.title: Level 3 · Data and special workloads
levels.summary: Keep data after restarts and run workloads that need stable names or one Pod per node.

lessons.title: Keep data after restarts
lessons.summary: EKS Auto Mode creates an Amazon EBS volume, so your data survives when a Pod restarts.

lessons.title: Reach every Pod directly
lessons.summary: A headless Service has no shared address. Looking up its name returns every Pod’s own address.

lessons.title: Databases with their own disks
lessons.summary: A StatefulSet gives each Pod a stable name and its own EBS volume.

lessons.title: Share files between Pods
lessons.summary: Mount one Amazon EFS file system in many Pods at once. Needs the EFS CSI add-on.

lessons.title: One Pod on every node
lessons.summary: A DaemonSet runs one copy of a Pod on each node, for example a log collector.

levels.title: Level 4 · Run safely
levels.summary: Share a cluster fairly, check that apps are healthy, and survive maintenance.

lessons.title: Default sizes for a namespace
lessons.summary: Set default and maximum CPU and memory for every container in a namespace.

lessons.title: A budget for a namespace
lessons.summary: Cap the total CPU and memory that all Pods in a namespace can ask for.

lessons.title: Is the app healthy?
lessons.summary: Let Kubernetes restart stuck containers and send traffic only to ready ones.

lessons.title: Start and stop timing
lessons.summary: Control how long Kubernetes waits when Pods start, roll out, and shut down.

lessons.title: Survive node maintenance
lessons.summary: Keep enough Pods running while nodes are drained for upgrades or repairs.

levels.title: Level 5 · Choose where Pods run
levels.summary: Steer Pods onto the right nodes and spread copies apart.

lessons.title: Pick nodes by label
lessons.summary: Run Pods only on nodes with the labels you choose.

lessons.title: Spread copies apart
lessons.summary: Keep copies of an app on different nodes, so one failure doesn't stop them all.

lessons.title: Keep Pods off some nodes
lessons.summary: Reserve nodes for special work. Only Pods that tolerate the taint can run there.

lessons.title: Choose your machines
lessons.summary: Tell EKS Auto Mode which kinds of machines it may launch for your Pods.

levels.title: Level 6 · Release new versions
levels.summary: Update apps safely with four common release strategies.

lessons.title: Rolling update
lessons.summary: Replace Pods a few at a time, so the app stays up during an update.

lessons.title: Stop, then start
lessons.summary: Stop every old Pod before starting new ones, for apps that cannot run two versions.

lessons.title: Blue-green
lessons.summary: Run the new version beside the old one, then switch all traffic at once.

lessons.title: Canary
lessons.summary: Send a small share of traffic to the new version before moving everyone.

levels.title: Level 7 · Scale
levels.summary: Add and remove Pods automatically as load changes.

lessons.title: Scale with load
lessons.summary: Add or remove Pods as CPU use goes up or down. Needs metrics-server installed.

levels.title: Level 8 · AWS access
levels.summary: Let Pods use AWS services without storing access keys.

lessons.title: Let a Pod call AWS safely
lessons.summary: Give a Pod its own AWS permissions through an IAM role, without storing access keys.

labs.title: Lab 1 · Hello Kubernetes
labs.summary: Deploy an app, scale it, and watch Kubernetes bring back a deleted Pod.

labs.title: Lab 2 · Your app on EKS
labs.cost: Uses your AWS account, which charges while the cluster runs
labs.summary: Run the same app on EKS Auto Mode with a load balancer and storage, then clean up.
